_comment: Master catalog of BUMP-confirmed behavioural breaks selected for this study. Each entry is anchored to a real BUMP TEST_FAILURE reproduction (breaking_commit -> data/benchmark_test_failures/<sha>.json + reproductionLogs/successfulReproductionLogs/<sha>.log). Use `bbc_pipeline.py characterize <breaking_commit>` to pull the exact failing test + exception, then derive a per-break spec in this folder. SHAs verified against data/benchmark_test_failures on 2026-07-06.
_provenance: MIXED SOURCES. Most entries are curated from BUMP (chains-project/breaking-updates), failureCategory=TEST_FAILURE, javaVersionUsedForReproduction=11 — these have a populated 'clients' array with breaking_commit(s). A GROWING MINORITY are EXTERNAL breaks mined from security advisories (OSV Maven feed via mine_advisories.py), NOT from BUMP: these carry a top-level "provenance":"EXTERNAL_ADVISORY_NOT_BUMP" flag plus an 'external_source' block, have an empty 'clients' array (no BUMP breaking_commit), and are found via 'mine-commits'+'classify' rather than 'characterize'/'run'.

breaks.why_it_breaks: commons-io 2.8.0 added strict input validation (FileUtils.requireFile). FileUtils.copyFile(srcFile, destFile) with a DIRECTORY as srcFile now throws an UNCHECKED java.lang.IllegalArgumentException ('Parameter 'srcFile' is not a file: <path>'), where <=2.7 threw a CHECKED IOException. Client code with catch(IOException) around copyFile no longer catches it, so the failure escapes to the production path.

characterization.signal: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Parameter 'srcFile' is not a file: <path> at org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils.requireFile / FileUtils.copyFile. commons-io 2.8+ throws unchecked IAE where 2.7 threw checked IOException.

breaks.why_it_breaks: Mockito 5.0 switched the default mock-maker to mockito-inline and tightened argument matching; verification/stubbing captures different args than under 4.x.

characterization.signal: java.lang.AssertionError: expected:<[3, 6]> but was:<[]> — Mockito 5 inline mock-maker changes shrinking/verification so the captured value differs.

breaks.why_it_breaks: Output/config behaviour change at the 1.4.0 Jakarta/Java-11 cutover (module rewrite; configuration + appender behaviour shifts).
breaks.note: Table listed the client as 'recheck'; the exact BUMP project is 'recheck.cli'. 'html2pop3' is another logback-classic client in BUMP (1.2.11->1.4.0 at 2b60dcd / 471b0bd) if a second client is wanted.

characterization.signal: java.lang.AssertionError — console/log output behaviour changed at the 1.4 cutover.

brief.what_changed: logback 1.4.0 moves to the SLF4J 2.x ServiceLoader binding and drops org.slf4j.impl.StaticLoggerBinder. A client still pinned to slf4j-api 1.7.x binds nothing: LoggerFactory silently falls back to a NOP logger, so logging output disappears rather than erroring. Where the old binder class is referenced directly, or a 1.7-era appender/config API is used, it fails harder.
brief.expected_signal_hint: logging output silently becomes empty (NOP logger substituted), or NoClassDefFoundError/ClassNotFoundException on org.slf4j.impl.StaticLoggerBinder, or an SLF4J binding warning on stderr instead of the expected log record

breaks.why_it_breaks: Logging output / binding behaviour changed across the 1.x -> 2.x rewrite (fluent API, ServiceLoader-based binding).
breaks.note: 'recheck' is a second slf4j client (1.7.36 -> 2.0.x) if wanted: 2.0.0 at 34e00b7, 2.0.3 at 0236320, etc.

characterization.signal: AssertionError [Expected ... ] — logged message format/binding changed across slf4j 1.x->2.x.

POI 5 extraction failures in fscrawler's Tika parser tests (see poi-ooxml note: crypt ClassNotFoundException / extractor change).

characterization.signal: org.junit.ComparisonFailure: reason-phrase formatting changed — 'status code: 400, reason phrase: ' now prefixes the message.

breaks.why_it_breaks: Parsing / output behaviour change at 1.15.0 (trailing whitespace trimmed after block open tags; shifts serialized/extracted text).

characterization.signal: java.lang.AssertionError (assertIsomorphic on RDF triples) — jsoup 1.15 trailing-whitespace trim shifts serialized output.

brief.what_changed: jsoup 1.15.x changed HTML output and text extraction behaviour: pretty-print indentation and whitespace normalisation were reworked, text-node trimming around inline/block boundaries changed, and Safelist/cleaning output shifted accordingly. Client code compiles unchanged; the break shows up as a different output string, not an exception. Adaptations typically switch to wholeText(), set outputSettings().prettyPrint(false) or indentAmount/maxPaddingWidth, or update expected strings.
brief.expected_signal_hint: an assertion failure (AssertionError / ComparisonFailure) on the exact HTML or extracted-text string produced by the client; whitespace, newlines or indentation differ; no exception is thrown

breaks.why_it_breaks: Security framework changed to default-deny at 1.4.18: unregistered classes now rejected on deserialization (ForbiddenClassException).

verify.signal_grep: ForbiddenClassException|NoTypePermission|security framework of XStream not initialized|no security framework configured

brief.what_changed: XStream changed its security model from a blacklist (deny a few known-dangerous types, allow everything else) to a whitelist (allow only a small set of built-in types, deny everything else). Client code that unmarshals its own domain types without first calling allowTypes / allowTypesByWildcard / addPermission still compiles and still marshals correctly, but now throws at unmarshal time. Marshalling (object -> XML) is unaffected; the break is on the read path.
brief.expected_signal_hint: com.thoughtworks.xstream.security.ForbiddenClassException (wrapped in a ConversionException / CannotResolveClassException) raised from fromXML/unmarshal on a client domain type
brief.signal_pattern: ForbiddenClassException|NoTypePermission|security framework of XStream not initialized|no security framework configured

breaks.why_it_breaks: 2.4.9 (CVE-2023-1370) added a maximum nesting-depth guard. Deeply-nested JSON that 2.4.8 parsed now throws net.minidev.json.parser.ParseException ('Malicious payload, having non natural depths'). Client code still compiles; it throws at runtime on previously-valid input -> semantic break.

characterization.signal: net.minidev.json.parser.ParseException: Malicious payload, having non natural depths, parsing stoped on { at position 14

mining.bump_axis_rationale: Added 2026-08-07. json-smart is the strongest untried lead in the census: 35 of its 43 resolvable candidate rows sit BELOW the 2.4.9 boundary (released 2023-03), so unlike org-json its client population can still cross. Until now it was mined on the adaptation axis only, which found 50 rows and 0 production adaptations -- the same result xstream gave before the bump axis took it from 20 candidates to 11 confirmed crossings. Its signal_quality is 'weak' precisely because the adaptation is config-shaped (setMaxDepth / input restructuring) and has no distinctive exception-handling idiom to search for; the bump axis does not depend on the adaptation having a searchable signature, which is why it is the right tool here. CVE-2023-1370 is the driver, so 'CVE' and 'security update' are live terms.

verify.note: NOT yet verified. Break is clean+deterministic (deeply-nested JSON). Adaptation is likely config/depth or input restructuring, so mining signature is weak; good agent target to attempt.

breaks.why_it_breaks: org.json tightened type coercion: JSONObject.getString() (and similar) on a non-string value (e.g. an Integer) now throws org.json.JSONException ('... is not a string') instead of coercing. Compiles fine; throws at runtime -> semantic break. Adaptation: use a coercing accessor (optString / String.valueOf(get(...))).

characterization.signal: org.json.JSONException: JSONObject["id"] is not a string (class java.lang.Integer : 0).

verify.note: Boundary pinned EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-04 by running JSONObject("{\"id\":0}").getString("id") against real jars: 20090211 COERCES (returns "0"); 20131018 and every later release THROW. The boundary is 20131018, not the catalogued to_version 20230227. Only the exception WORDING changed after that: '... not a string.' (<=20190722) -> '... is not a string' (20200518+) -> '... is not a string (class java.lang.Integer : 0)' (20220924+). Previously this field read 'the release that added strict getString coercion', which has no digits, so _parse_ver returned None and _crosses_boundary was False for EVERY candidate — traversal could never confirm anything for this break, silently.

yield_status.reason: The boundary is 20131018 (Oct 2013). Every one of the 31 mined production adaptations that has a resolved version is above it (earliest 20160810), so no mineable client can have crossed it — they are all born past the boundary. The adaptations are real responses to org.json's strictness, but not to a transition the client lived through.
yield_status.implication: A break is only mineable for witnessed crossings if the boundary is recent enough that clients still cross it. Check the boundary DATE before mining, not just its existence.

breaks.why_it_breaks: H2 2.0 was a major SQL-compatibility overhaul (new reserved keywords, stricter typing/casting, changed defaults). Queries/schema that worked on 1.x now fail at runtime (surfaces here as org.hibernate...SqlException). Compiles fine -> semantic break. Adaptation: MODE=LEGACY or NON_KEYWORDS=... in the JDBC URL, or rename reserved-word columns.

verify.note: NOT yet verified. Framework-mediated (Hibernate) + adaptation often config (JDBC URL MODE/NON_KEYWORDS) or schema; may need the app's DB. Medium priority.

yield_status.can_yield_BBC_cases: ALMOST NEVER — a COMPILE break masks the behavioural one for most clients
yield_status.reason: snakeyaml 2.0 removed EVERY constructor overload that does not take a LoaderOptions. Measured with javap: Constructor at 1.32 offers (), (LoaderOptions), (Class), (Class, LoaderOptions), (TypeDescription); at 2.0 ONLY the LoaderOptions-bearing variants survive. SafeConstructor at 1.32 offers () and (LoaderOptions); at 2.0 only (LoaderOptions). So any client that explicitly constructs a Constructor or SafeConstructor — the common 1.x idiom — fails at javac when it crosses to 2.x and NEVER REACHES the runtime tag-inspection change. The behavioural break is real but is shadowed by a syntactic one on the same classes.
yield_status.who_can_still_witness_it: Only clients that never construct a Constructor/SafeConstructor explicitly — i.e. plain `new Yaml()` — compile cleanly at 2.x and can therefore hit the deny-by-default tag behaviour at runtime. That is the snakeyaml-mongoose / KartaEmeraldCurrency idiom, and those clients were already on 2.x (born past the boundary), which is why they sit in excluded/mechanism_only/.
yield_status.evidence: All THREE traversal-confirmed candidates found across both mining axes are compile breaks: adityajoy-1902/Dashboard-V-2 (Constructor(Class) narrowed to Constructor(LoaderOptions)), snork-alt/beanszoo (no-arg super() on a Constructor subclass), GoogleCloudPlatform/appengine-plugins (no-arg SafeConstructor()). Three for three, three different removed overloads.
yield_status.implication: A break is only mineable for BBC cases if the same release does not also break compilation on the API the break lives behind. Check the boundary version for REMOVED/NARROWED signatures on the affected classes before mining — screen_compile_break.py answers this from jars alone, with no client build, and would have predicted this corpus's outcome before any of the mining was done.

breaks._provenance_note: This entry is NOT from BUMP. It was discovered by mine_advisories.py from the OSV Maven security-advisory feed (GHSA-mjmj-j48q-9wg2 / CVE-2022-1471), NOT from a BUMP TEST_FAILURE reproduction. There is no BUMP breaking_commit; 'clients' is empty until mining finds real client adaptations.
breaks.why_it_breaks: snakeyaml 2.0 (CVE-2022-1471) makes SafeConstructor the effective default via a restrictive LoaderOptions TagInspector: new Yaml().load(...) no longer instantiates arbitrary Java types from YAML global tags. YAML that maps to application types (custom '!!com.example.Foo' tags) that 1.x deserialized now throws at load time. Client code still compiles; it throws at runtime on previously-accepted input -> semantic break. Adaptation: pass an explicit Constructor, or configure LoaderOptions.setTagInspector(tag -> tag.getClassName().equals(...)) / a trusted-tag inspector to re-allow the needed types.

Real signature_confirmed clients: telaminai/mongoose-plugins@9e5916e1, Minekarta-Studio/KartaEmeraldCurrency@8bb46ffa, quarkusio/quarkus@06a8c629. Mining yield: 275 commits / 199 repos. characterization.signal: org.yaml.snakeyaml.constructor.ConstructorException / YAMLException: 'Global tag is not allowed' (or 'could not determine a constructor for the tag') — 2.0 restrictive TagInspector rejects arbitrary-type YAML that 1.x accepted.
characterization.note: Characterization derived from the advisory + the known 2.0 API change, NOT a BUMP repro log. Confirm the exact exception message at verify time.

trigger.description: A GLOBAL tag naming a Java class (e.g. !!com.example.Foo). snakeyaml 2.0's default TagInspector rejects exactly these. Requiring a dot excludes the standard YAML tags (!!str, !!int, !!map), which are never rejected. LOCAL tags (single !, resolved from the constructor's own yamlConstructors map) also do NOT reach the inspector, so they must not match.
trigger.note: A client whose YAML contains no global tag cannot experience this break, however cleanly it compiles and however real its bump. Verified on adityajoy-1902/Dashboard-V-2: root-type Constructor(Application.class) with tag-free YAML -> the adaptation was purely a compile migration.
trigger.unknown_if: YAML is supplied at runtime rather than bundled in the repo; then the trigger is undecidable from source.

verify.signal_grep: Global tag is not allowed|ConstructorException|could not determine a constructor
verify.note: VERIFIED — see verify_status (3-state differential green 2026-07-20). Clean default-deny (direct xstream analogue). Adaptation = explicit Constructor / LoaderOptions.setTagInspector. First EXTERNAL-mined break fed through the pipeline.

breaks.rejection_finding: Investigated 2026-07-20 (mined 241 commits/208 repos; inspected real diffs incl. madgeek-arc/resource-catalogue@7f625e24, omprakash201194/kin-keeper@89eb519c). Jackson default-typing does NOT exhibit the 'same code, new version, now throws' property: (1) the permissive idiom enableDefaultTyping()/LaissezFaire stayed permissive through the deprecation window; (2) BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator/activateDefaultTyping appear overwhelmingly in Spring Redis-cache serialization config (greenfield — modern jackson requires a PTV there by design) and in iterative allowlist tuning, NOT version-upgrade break fixes; (3) remaining hits are CVE dependency-bumps (no code change) and Jackson 2->3 migrations. Sits on the BLOCKLIST/API-MIGRATION side of the deserialize tier, not the DEFAULT-DENY side. Kept as a documented NEGATIVE result. Do not re-attempt.
breaks._provenance_note: NOT from BUMP. Discovered by mine_advisories.py from the OSV Maven advisory feed (jackson-databind CWE-502 default-typing / polymorphic-deserialization CVE series). No BUMP breaking_commit; clients empty until mining finds real adaptations.
breaks.why_it_breaks: jackson 2.10 locked down polymorphic default typing (CVE series). enableDefaultTyping() was deprecated in favour of activateDefaultTyping(PolymorphicTypeValidator); polymorphic deserialization of types not permitted by the validator throws com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.InvalidDefinitionException / InvalidTypeIdException at runtime. Adaptation: supply a BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator allowlist. TO BE CONFIRMED from real diffs — jackson default-typing has an API-migration confound (enableDefaultTyping deprecated 2.10, removed 2.12), so verify the actual break shape before designing the differential.

breaks._provenance_note: NOT from BUMP and NOT from the CVE advisory feed. This is external-mining discovery SOURCE #2 (library changelog / release notes): jackson-core 2.15.0 added StreamReadConstraints default parser limits. A genuine 'same code, new version, now throws' behavioural break (the clean jackson break, unlike the REJECTED default-typing one). No BUMP breaking_commit; clients found via mine-commits.
breaks.why_it_breaks: jackson-core 2.15.0 introduced StreamReadConstraints with default parser limits: maxNestingDepth=1000, maxNumberLength=1000, maxNameLength, maxStringLength (5M in 2.15.0, 20M in 2.15.1+). JSON exceeding a limit that 2.14 parsed fine now throws com.fasterxml.jackson.core.exc.StreamConstraintsException at parse time. Code compiles unchanged; it throws at runtime on previously-accepted input -> behavioural break. Adaptation: build a JsonFactory with relaxed StreamReadConstraints, e.g. JsonFactory.builder().streamReadConstraints(StreamReadConstraints.builder().maxNestingDepth(N).maxStringLength(N).build()).build().

external_source.discovered_via: domain knowledge / release notes (external-mining source #2), NOT the CVE advisory miner

breaks.verify_status: VERIFIED_BBC 2026-07-20 — 3-state differential green (2.14.2 PASS / 2.15.0 FAIL 'StreamConstraintsException: Depth (1001) exceeds the maximum allowed nesting depth (1000)' / adapted PASS) on scratchpad/jackson-streamconstraints-harness. Real signature_confirmed clients: dotCMS/core@b30dfa31, cibseven/cibseven@81a8d2b2, centiservice/mats3@79e05ec1, ESSI-Lab/DAB@9385e949. Mining yield: 184 commits / 159 repos.

verify.note: Clean same-code-now-throws limit break (json-smart max-depth analogue). Parent uses plain new ObjectMapper() (stable across 2.14/2.15); adapted uses the 2.15-only StreamReadConstraints API (separate compile profile).

breaks._provenance_note: From the OSV Maven feed (GHSA-pv7h-hx5h-mgfj / CVE-2022-25845), selected by rank_candidates.py 2026-08-07 as the highest-scoring deserialize-tier library that passes BOTH structural filters: boundary released 2022-05 (recent enough that clients still cross it, unlike org-json) and ZERO public API removed between 1.2.80 and 1.2.83 (so no compile break shadows the behavioural one, unlike snakeyaml). First non-xstream library to clear every filter.
breaks.why_it_breaks: 1.2.83 (CVE-2022-25845) tightens autoType: deserializing a JSON document carrying an @type tag into an arbitrary class is refused unless the type is explicitly permitted. Client code still COMPILES -- no signature changed, confirmed by a javap API diff showing 0 removals -- and throws at runtime on documents 1.2.80 accepted. The adaptation is an explicit re-permit: ParserConfig.getGlobalInstance().addAccept("com.foo."), setAutoTypeSupport(true), or safeMode configuration. Structurally the same shape as xstream allowTypes, which is the only shape that has yielded verified cases.

verify.note: NOT yet verified. Break is deny-by-default autoType; adaptation is an explicit allowlist call, the cleanest mining signature after xstream.

breaks._provenance_note: From the OSV Maven feed (GHSA-6phf-73q6-gh87 / CVE-2019-10086), selected by rank_candidates.py 2026-08-09. Passes every structural filter: boundary 2019-07 (old enough that clients have genuinely crossed, unlike the 2026 Camel entries), ZERO public API removed 1.9.3 -> 1.9.4 per javap diff (no compile break to shadow the behaviour, unlike snakeyaml), and it is ordinary infrastructure coded against directly by thousands of applications (unlike json-smart, which is transitive, and unlike fastjson, whose corpus is dominated by exploit demos).
breaks.why_it_breaks: 1.9.4 (CVE-2019-10086) registers SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector.SUPPRESS_CLASS by DEFAULT, so the bean property named "class" is no longer introspectable. BOUNDARY PINNED EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-09 by running PropertyUtils.getProperty(bean, "class") against both jars on JDK 11: 1.9.3 returns the Class object; 1.9.4 throws NoSuchMethodException ("Unknown property class on class ..."). The class SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector exists in BOTH jars -- only the default registration changed -- so client code COMPILES unchanged and fails at run time. Deny-by-default with an explicit re-permit, structurally the same as xstream allowTypes: PropertyUtils.getPropertyUtils().removeBeanIntrospector(SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector.SUPPRESS_CLASS).

verify.note: Boundary pinned empirically (see why_it_breaks). Probe: PropertyUtils.getProperty(bean,"class") returns on 1.9.3, throws on 1.9.4.
